sections.h2: Which Cherry Hill office sends the tax bill
sections.html:
Property tax in Cherry Hill is billed and collected by the township's Tax Collector, who also runs the township sewer accounts. The office is in Room 108 of the municipal building at 820 Mercer Street, and the phone is 856-488-7880. It also acts as the collecting agent for the public school district, the fire district and Camden County, so one bill covers all of them.

Value is a separate matter. The township assessor sets assessments, appeals go to the Camden County Board of Taxation in Blackwood, and the collector has no role in them. The township's main number is 856-665-6500, and the assessor and collector both work from 820 Mercer Street. The collector tells you what you owe. The assessor and county board tell you whether the value behind it can be challenged.

The township spreads over 24.07 square miles in northern Camden County and had an estimated 79,965 residents in 2025. Home values center on $386,300, and 76.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Neighborhood names buyers search by include Erlton, Barclay, Kingston, Greentree, Springdale, Old Orchard, Woodcrest and Ellisburg.

Interstate 295 has three exits in the township, and Routes 38, 41, 70 and 154 cross it. The PATCO station at Woodcrest and NJ Transit's Atlantic City Line stop give commuters a route into Philadelphia. The school district runs 19 schools, which is a draw for families and shows up in how listings are marketed.

sections.h2: Due dates, interest and where the money goes
sections.html:
The township's quarterly dates are August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. A ten-day cushion follows each one, and a tenth day that falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday carries the cushion to the next working day. The office mails bills twice a year: in July for the third and fourth quarters and in January for the first and second. A bill that never shows up does not cancel the payment or the interest.

Money has to reach the office before the grace period ends, because New Jersey does not allow the collector to accept postmarks. Once the cushion ends, interest is charged retroactively: 8 percent annually on the first slice of $1,500 behind, 18 percent annually on the remainder. Balances still open can move into the tax sale process, which has to be finished by June 30, and payments during that period must be cash or a cashier's check.

sections.h2: How to pay a tax or sewer bill
sections.html:
The township accepts payment five ways. If you use your bank's bill-pay service, schedule it five business days ahead, since some banks send a paper check.

  • Drop off cash or a check at Room 108, or use the mail slot on the double doors at the entrance if the building is closed.
  • Mail a check to the Tax Collector's Office, 820 Mercer Street, Cherry Hill, NJ 08002.
  • Use the online portal with a card or e-check. The processor, not the township, adds 2.39 percent on cards and 99 cents on an e-check.
  • Use your bank's bill-pay with "Township of Cherry Hill" as payee and your numeric account number only.
  • Pay by phone: 855-472-2993 for taxes and 855-472-2990 for sewer.

The counter and the staff phone line do not take cards. The office also sends email reminders about a week before each due date to residents who sign up.

sections.h2: Sewer charges and the senior discount
sections.html: A flat annual fee covers residential sewer and falls due April 1. Commercial sewer follows water use and is billed in two parts, due the first of November and the first of May. A 10 percent reduction is available to owners aged 60 and up who live in the house and show the Tax Collector proof of age. Sewer is billed apart from tax, so the closing agent should ask the collector whether it is paid to date.

sections.h2: Is a Cherry Hill assessment open to challenge?
sections.html:
Yes. Camden County's tax board hears the case, with filing closing April 1 or, right after a township revaluation, May 1. The petition has to reach the county before close of business that day, and installments through the first quarter stay payable while the case is open. Evidence is up to five comparable sales, since neighbors' assessments carry no weight. With the average assessment at $227,000, you have a yardstick when you compare your notice to the street around you.

Appeal only the value, never the amount of tax. Your argument is what the house was worth on the October 1 that precedes the tax year, set against the town's average ratio. If the county board lowers the value, that judgment holds for the year and the two that follow unless a revaluation or an added assessment changes it. After the board rules, the Tax Court of New Jersey takes any further case, filed within 45 days.

A sale can go ahead with tax owing, because the balance is cleared out of the seller's money at the table. Request a payoff statement dated for your closing day, and hand the latest bill to the title company so the next installment goes to the right place.

  • Look at where your closing date sits against the next quarter and its cushion.
  • Confirm the sewer account is paid to date.
  • If a lien has been sold at the tax sale, the lien holder is the party owed the redemption amount.

A cash sale does not change any of this. It only removes the lender's appraisal and most repairs, so the payoff letters and the sewer check become the main items on your list.

sections.h2: Getting ready to sell a Cherry Hill house
sections.html:
Order the tax payoff and the sewer status together, since both come from the same office. Compare your assessment notice with the house, and check the date of the next quarter against your closing date. If the closing falls near a due date, ask the closing agent whether to pay the installment first or have it handled from your proceeds.

Keep the latest bill, because the title company needs it to place the next installment. If you are 60 or older and live in the house, carry proof of age to the collector so the sewer discount is not lost in the transition.

faqs.q: What is the grace period for Cherry Hill property tax?
faqs.a: Ten days from each due date, stretched past a weekend or holiday to the next working day. The office has to have the money in hand by then, as postmarks carry no weight.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Cherry Hill taxes?
faqs.a: Pay at the Tax Collector's Office, 820 Mercer Street, Room 108, by mail, online, by phone or through bank bill-pay. Call 856-488-7880 for help.

faqs.q: Does Cherry Hill offer a sewer discount for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. A 10 percent cut on the residential sewer fee goes to owner-occupants aged 60 or more who show proof of age.

faqs.q: How much interest does Cherry Hill charge on late tax?
faqs.a: Eight percent per year covers the first $1,500 late and 18 percent the rest, charged back to the original due date.

faqs.q: Who hears a Cherry Hill assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The county board in Blackwood, at 509 Lakeland Road. Filing closes April 1, or May 1 when the township has just completed a revaluation.
